summary: Default `sync` (no --resources) re-scrapes what the store already knows — every watchlist entry (with its saved dates) and every previously-scraped airbnb_listing, de-duplicated by URL — and persists fresh price snapshots via the same best-effort scrape-persist path. An empty store is reported honestly (sync_warning reason=empty_store) with NO network call, never a 404. The authenticated Airbnb wishlist sync is preserved as an explicitly opt-in, auth-gated resource: `sync --resources airbnb_wishlist` routes to airbnb.WishlistList behind 'auth login --chrome' and surfaces an auth error (not a 404) when cookies are missing. Any other explicitly-named resource still flows through the legacy API-mirror syncResource engine.
reason: Airbnb has no public paginated collection, so the generated default (defaultSyncResources -> ['airbnb_wishlist'] -> syncResourcePath -> a GraphQL persisted-query path) 404s/auth-gates on every default run. A scraper's 'sync' must mean 'refresh what you've already seen', driving off store state (ListWatchlist + the airbnb_listing table) rather than a remote cursor. The auth-gated wishlist path (airbnb.WishlistList, cookie jar) is real functionality and must NOT be deleted — it stays selectable and documented-as-requiring-auth. The legacy syncResource/syncResourcePath machinery is kept intact because the auto-refresh hook still uses it for the airbnb_wishlist read paths. A regen must keep the default as a store-driven re-scrape with an honest empty-store report, and keep the auth-gated wishlist resource selectable.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test green. collectScrapeTargets test: empty store yields zero targets; watchlist + known listings are gathered and de-duplicated by URL with watchlist dates winning. Live smoke: sync against an empty isolated store emitted sync_warning reason=empty_store and made no network call (exit 0); sync against a store seeded with one known listing re-scraped it and persisted a snapshot.
